Jurisdiction

The Gloucester City Municipal Court operates under Camden County, New Jersey. It handles a range of cases, including criminal offenses, disorderly person offenses, traffic violations, speeding cases, and city housing code violations. Under the New Jersey Motor Vehicle Law, all traffic-related violations are processed through this court. Regular court sessions are held every Tuesday at 8:30 pm. Proper attire is required during court hearings.

Virtual Court Hearings

Gloucester City Municipal Court offers virtual hearings through Zoom, a practice adopted during the COVID-19 pandemic. Participants will receive an email with a meeting link to join the court hearing. Ensure a strong internet connection and proper dressing, as well as functioning audio and video capabilities. It is advised to join the meeting 10 minutes early.

Traffic Court Cases

The Gloucester City Municipal Court manages various traffic offenses, including but not limited to:

  • Driving with a suspended or expired license
  • Reckless driving or driving under the influence of drugs
  • Speeding violations
  • Operating vehicles without plates
  • Ignoring traffic control devices and signs
  • Failing to stop at red lights or stop signs
  • Not wearing seat belts
  • Using mobile phones while driving

If you receive a ticket, you must enter a plea and submit it to the court before the citation date. Attendance in court may be necessary depending on the type of violation.

Submitting a Plea by Mail

Plea submissions to the Gloucester City Municipal Court can be made for traffic infractions, speeding, or parking tickets. Complete a plea form and send it before the citation date. You can choose from two types of pleas:

  • Plea of Guilty: If you admit to the violation, the court will review your plea and provide information regarding fines or court dates.
  • Plea of Not Guilty: If you dispute the charges, submit a not guilty plea. The court will schedule a hearing, where you will need to present evidence in your defense. Consider hiring an attorney for assistance.

Consequences of Non-Appearance

Attendance at the Gloucester City Municipal Court is mandatory for specific cases. Failing to appear can lead to additional charges, suspension of your driver's license or insurance, and, in severe cases, an arrest warrant. Additionally, penalties may apply for late parking ticket payments. For assistance, contact the court during operating hours.

How to Change Court Date in Jersey City

To change a court date in Jersey City, you typically need to file a motion with the court where your case is pending. Here’s how to do it:

  1. Contact the Court: Call or visit the court to inform them that you wish to change your court date.
  2. File a Motion: You may need to complete a form or write a letter requesting a new court date. Be sure to include your case number and the reasons for the change.
  3. Submit the Motion: File the motion with the court clerk’s office. Ensure you do this well in advance of your scheduled court date.
  4. Notify Other Parties: If applicable, inform the prosecutor or other parties involved in your case about the request for a new date.

When Was Gloucester City, NJ Founded?

Gloucester City, NJ, was founded in 1868. It was originally part of the larger Gloucester Township before becoming its own municipality. The city has a rich history tied to its location along the Delaware River, which played a significant role in its development.
